\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2010 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 6}

Two particles move along the \(x\)-axis. For \(0 \leq t \leq 6\), the position of particle \(P\) at time \(t\) is given by \(p(t)=2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4} t\right)\), while the position of particle \(R\) at time \(t\) is given by \(r(t)=t^{3}-6 t^{2}+9 t+3\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] For \(0 \leq t \leq 6\), find all times \(t\) during which particle \(R\) is moving to the right.
\item[(b)] For \(0 \leq t \leq 6\), find all times \(t\) during which the two particles travel in opposite directions.
\item[(c)] Find the acceleration of particle \(P\) at time \(t=3\). Is particle \(P\) speeding up, slowing down, or doing neither at time \(t=3\) ? Explain your reasoning.
\item[(d)] Write, but do not evaluate, an expression for the average distance between the two particles on the interval \(1 \leq t \leq 3\).
\item[(a)] \(r^{\prime}(t)=3 t^{2}-12 t+9=3(t-1)(t-3)\)
\(r^{\prime}(t)=0\) when \(t=1\) and \(t=3\)
\(r^{\prime}(t)>0\) for \(0<t<1\) and \(3<t<6\)
\(r^{\prime}(t)<0\) for \(1<t<3\)
Therefore \(R\) is moving to the right for \(0<t<1\) and \(3<t<6\).
\item[(b)] \(p^{\prime}(t)=-2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{4} \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4} t\right)\)
\(p^{\prime}(t)=0\) when \(t=0\) and \(t=4\)
\(p^{\prime}(t)<0\) for \(0<t<4\)
\(p^{\prime}(t)>0\) for \(4<t<6\)
Therefore the particles travel in opposite directions for \(0<t<1\) and \(3<t<4\).
\item[(c)] \(p^{\prime \prime}(t)=-2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \frac{\pi}{4} \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4} t\right)\)
\(p^{\prime \prime}(3)=-2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2} \cos \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi^{2}}{8} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}>0\)
\(p^{\prime}(3)<0\)
Therefore particle \(P\) is slowing down at time \(t=3\).
\item[(d)] \(\frac{1}{2} \int_{1}^{3}|p(t)-r(t)| d t\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: r^{\prime}(t) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: p^{\prime}(t) \\ 1: \text { sign analysis for } p^{\prime}(t) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: p^{\prime \prime}(3) \\ 1: \text { answer with reason }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { limits and constant }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
